title: Responsive/device emulation
learningObjectives: Explain responsive/device emulation and use browser or version-control tools to diagnose and publish reliable web projects.

understand.concept: Responsive design tools let developers emulate viewport dimensions, device pixel ratio, touch input, and sometimes network or CPU conditions. Emulation is useful but does not perfectly reproduce every real device or browser.
understand.whyItMatters: Testing several viewport sizes reveals overflow, clipped controls, and layout breakpoints. Real-device testing is still important for touch, performance, and platform-specific behaviour.
understand.analogy: Device emulation is a test bench that approximates different screen and input conditions.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; actual developer tools, Git behaviour, and deployment requirements depend on the browser, repository, and hosting provider.

explain.narrative: The code reports the current viewport width. Developer tools let you change emulated dimensions and inspect responsive behaviour.

examples.explanation: The code reports the current viewport width. Developer tools let you change emulated dimensions and inspect responsive behaviour.
examples.expectedOutput: The example illustrates the workflow or developer-tool concept; command examples require a practice repository.

practise.guidedTask: Test a page at narrow, medium, and wide viewports. Check horizontal overflow, navigation, and long translated text.
practise.independentTask: Apply the workflow to a small static site. Capture the commands or browser evidence, identify risks, and document recovery steps.
hints: Inspect actual files and browser behaviour.
Do not commit secrets or personal data.
Verify provider-specific deployment values before changing DNS.
